# LayoutProposal

A change an agent proposes to the surface the person is using (a layout, a set of columns, an arrangement), which the person previews, then applies or discards. It says who proposed it, when and why, with a sketch of the change, and Preview, Apply and Discard. Preview turns into "Back to current" in place, so focus stays on the button, and screen readers hear that nothing changes until the person applies it. Applying and discarding are a person's decisions: the handlers receive the click event, so the app can check `event.isTrusted`, and the proposal's `id` as it was when the press began, so the app can refuse a decision about a proposal that was replaced under the person's pointer.

```tsx
import { LayoutProposal } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/layout-proposal/layout-proposal";
```

## Example

```tsx
<LayoutProposal
  id={proposal.id}
  title="Customers first"
  by="Ouro"
  reason="You open customer chats first most mornings."
  previewing={previewing}
  onPreview={() => setPreviewing(true)}
  onEndPreview={() => setPreviewing(false)}
  onApply={(id, event) => event.isTrusted && id === proposal.id && apply(id)}
  onDiscard={(id, event) => event.isTrusted && id === proposal.id && discard(id)}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Alert` instead for a notice that asks for no decision, and `DraftReview` for changes to text that are accepted one by one.

## Props

Type: `LayoutProposalProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `applyLabel` | `string` | `"Apply"` | The Apply button's word, for other languages. |
| `by` (required) | `string` |  | Who proposed it, usually the agent's name ("Ouro"). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | A sketch or summary of the change, such as the proposed columns. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-2`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `discardLabel` | `string` | `"Discard"` | The Discard button's word, for other languages. |
| `endPreviewLabel` | `string` | `"Back to current"` | The button that ends the preview, for other languages. |
| `id` (required) | `string` |  | Identifies the proposal. The handlers receive the `id` that was on screen when the person began the press, so the app can refuse a decision about a proposal it has since replaced. |
| `onApply` (required) | `LayoutProposalHandler` |  | Called when the person applies the proposal. Applying is a person's decision: check `event.isTrusted`, and that `id` is still the proposal you hold, before you apply it. |
| `onDiscard` (required) | `LayoutProposalHandler` |  | Called when the person discards the proposal, with the same checks as `onApply`. |
| `onEndPreview` | `LayoutProposalHandler` |  | Ends the preview and returns to the current arrangement. Needed with `onPreview`. |
| `onPreview` | `LayoutProposalHandler` |  | Adds Preview, which shows the proposal in place without applying it. |
| `previewing` | `boolean` | `false` | The proposal is on screen in place of the current arrangement. |
| `previewingLabel` | `string` | `"Previewing"` | The badge while previewing, for other languages. |
| `previewLabel` | `string` | `"Preview"` | The Preview button's word, for other languages. |
| `previewNote` | `string` | `"This is a preview. Nothing changes until you apply it."` | The line shown, and spoken, while previewing. |
| `proposedLabel` | `string` | `"Proposed change"` | The badge, for other languages. |
| `reason` | `ReactNode` |  | Why, in a sentence from whoever proposed it. Hidden while previewing. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `time` | `ReactNode` |  | When, already formatted ("2 min ago", `<RelativeTime>`). |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | What the change is, in a few words ("Customers first"). |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `note`: Not a prop. The reason is `reason`: `<LayoutProposal reason="You open customer chats first.">`.
- `onAccept`: Not a prop. Applying calls `onApply`: `<LayoutProposal onApply={(id, event) => apply(id, event)}>`.
- `onBack`: Not a prop. Ending the preview calls `onEndPreview`: `<LayoutProposal onEndPreview={(id) => endPreview(id)}>`.
- `onDismiss`: Not a prop. Discarding calls `onDiscard`: `<LayoutProposal onDiscard={(id) => discard(id)}>`.
- `onReject`: Not a prop. Discarding calls `onDiscard`: `<LayoutProposal onDiscard={(id) => discard(id)}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: LayoutProposal merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `LayoutProposalHandler`

A decision about a proposal: its `id` as it was when the person began the press, and the click.

```ts
type LayoutProposalHandler = (id: string, event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement>) => void;
```
